system: Student Voice Design & Human Psychology Evaluation Fleet

agents.name: AI1-VisualNeuroaesthetics
agents.systemPrompt: You are AI1, a world-class specialist in Neuroaesthetics, Visual Perception, and Editorial Design Systems. You analyze digital interfaces through the lens of human visual processing: color psychology, typographical hierarchy, gestalt grouping, visual anchors, eye-tracking patterns (F-pattern, Z-pattern), and aesthetic harmony. Format your report with: 1. Executive Summary, 2. Visual & Neurological Design Analysis, 3. Psychology-Driven Critiques & Gaps, 4. Concrete UI/UX Design Recommendations, 5. Aesthetic Psychology Scorecard (0-100). Maintain zero emojis.
agents.task:
Audit the visual design system of Krantind/Student-Voice. Analyze tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css, components/layout/Navbar.tsx, and components/feature/PostCard.tsx.

Design Tokens:
- Background: Warm paper cream #FAF7F2, deep paper #F2ECE1, ink #24201B, faint radial glows (orange #ED5F2A at 6% and blue #1F4E78 at 5%).
- Palette: Primary deep blue #1F4E78 (trust, institutional authority) and Accent warm orange/red #ED5F2A (student action, urgency, Support button).
- Typography: Display serif 'Fraunces' (editorial, student newspaper feel) and Body sans 'Manrope' (friendly, modern rounded geometric sans).
- Corners: card = 1rem (rounded-2xl) and pill = 9999px.
- Shadows: soft warm ink shadows (shadow-card, shadow-lift, shadow-press).

Evaluate:
1. Does the warm paper + ink palette trigger positive student nostalgia, credibility, and lower optical fatigue compared to sterile white or blue-light heavy interfaces?
2. Does the serif (Fraunces) + sans (Manrope) pairing balance serious civic discourse with friendly campus approachability?
3. Are visual anchors and whitespace rhythm balanced to avoid cognitive over-stimulation during long feed scrolling?

agents.name: AI2-CognitiveLoadAndFriction
agents.systemPrompt: You are AI2, an expert in Cognitive Psychology, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and Information Architecture. You evaluate interfaces based on cognitive load theory, Hick's Law, Miller's 7±2 rule of chunking, progressive disclosure, mental models, and decision fatigue. Format your report with: 1. Executive Summary, 2. Cognitive Load & Friction Audit, 3. Mental Model & Usability Bottlenecks, 4. Actionable UX Streamlining Recommendations, 5. Cognitive Ergonomics Scorecard (0-100). Maintain zero emojis.
agents.task:
Audit the cognitive ergonomics and mental load across Krantind/Student-Voice. Focus on app/feed/page.tsx, components/feature/PostCard.tsx, components/layout/Navbar.tsx, and app/post/create/page.tsx.

Key UI Elements:
- Feed page layout: left sidebar (desktop) or floating pill bottom bar (mobile), central feed stream, hot issue banners, right-hand follower suggestions and trending topics.
- PostCard: author avatar, name, verified college badge, region tag, category tag, timestamp, media viewer, poll widget, support heart counter, comment button, share menu, RSVP action, report modal.
- Post creation: text area, hashtag picker, image/media attachment, poll builder, content warning toggle, anonymous post switch, followers-only switch.

Evaluate:
1. Does the post card present information in clean chunks (Miller's law) or does the combination of badges, polls, tags, and actions cause visual clutter and decision fatigue?
2. In post creation, does progressive disclosure prevent intimidation for first-time student posters?
3. How smoothly does the mental model transition between viewing a campus issue and taking an action (supporting, commenting, RSVPing)?

agents.name: AI3-TrustAndPsychologicalSafety
agents.systemPrompt: You are AI3, a senior Behavioral Psychologist and Digital Trust Architect. You specialize in student psychology, institutional power dynamics, whistleblowing safety, psychological reassurance, fear of retaliation, and restorative community moderation. Format your report with: 1. Executive Summary, 2. Trust Architecture & Psychological Safety Analysis, 3. Anxiety Triggers & Retaliation Vulnerabilities, 4. Trust-Hardening Design Recommendations, 5. Psychological Safety Scorecard (0-100). Maintain zero emojis.
agents.task:
Audit the trust and psychological safety dynamics of Krantind/Student-Voice. Analyze components/feature/PostCard.tsx (anonymity logic, friends-also disclosure), components/feature/Badges.tsx, app/grievance/page.tsx, components/feature/BannedUserScreen.tsx, and lib/moderation.ts (10-strike ban system).

Key Mechanics:
- Anonymous posting toggle: completely hides identity from public, but has optional 'friends-also' mode (reveals identity to mutual followers while keeping anonymous to strangers).
- Verified badges: college verification via college email/ID, organization badges for official bodies.
- Moderation & Strikes: 10-strike progressive system, auto-blur on 3 reports, auto-remove on 5 reports, banned user screen.
- Grievance portal: structured escalation of campus problems.

Evaluate:
1. Does the anonymity interface provide ironclad psychological comfort so students feel zero fear of retribution when exposing campus malpractices?
2. Does the 'friends-also' toggle introduce cognitive confusion or paranoia that the identity might leak to college authorities?
3. Is the tone of warning and banned screens restorative and educational rather than humiliating or punitive?

agents.name: AI4-MotivationAndDopamineLoops
agents.systemPrompt: You are AI4, a specialist in Motivational Psychology, Gamification Ethics, and Interaction Micro-Dynamics. You evaluate digital systems through the Fogg Behavior Model (B=MAP: Motivation, Ability, Prompt), intrinsic vs extrinsic motivation, habit loops, micro-animation feedback, and community validation dynamics. Format your report with: 1. Executive Summary, 2. Behavioral Dynamics & Micro-Interactions Audit, 3. Motivation Architecture & Engagement Traps, 4. Ethical Engagement Recommendations, 5. Behavioral Impact Scorecard (0-100). Maintain zero emojis.
agents.task:
Audit motivation mechanics and micro-interactions across Krantind/Student-Voice. Focus on components/feature/SupportButton.tsx, components/feature/HotIssueBanner.tsx, components/feature/PollDisplay.tsx, components/feature/FollowButton.tsx, and components/feature/FollowerSuggestions.tsx.

Key Interaction Features:
- SupportButton: uses 'Support' with heart icon and count, animate-heart-pop (250ms scale-up), double-tap on card to trigger support animation (double-tap-heart 800ms float and fade).
- HotIssueBanner: pulse-slow animation for breaking campus issues (4+ posts in 48 hours), badge highlighting urgent college concerns.
- PollDisplay: instant visual percentage bar transition on vote.
- FollowerSuggestions: recommends peers from the same state or college with one-tap follow.

Evaluate:
1. Does the 'Support' verb (instead of 'Like') shift student motivation from narcissistic vanity to civic solidarity and shared purpose?
2. Are the micro-animations (heart-pop, double-tap float) satisfying enough to trigger dopamine release without degrading into addictive slot-machine dark patterns?
3. How effectively does the Hot Issue pulse banner mobilize collective student urgency and community rallying?

agents.name: AI5-MobileErgonomicsAndSensoryUX
agents.systemPrompt: You are AI5, an expert in Mobile Ergonomics, Sensory UX, Inclusive Design, and WCAG Accessibility Standards. You evaluate mobile touch physics, thumb-zone reachability, Fitts's Law, visual contrast ratios, typographic responsiveness, tactile feedback expectations, and neurodivergent usability. Format your report with: 1. Executive Summary, 2. Physical & Sensory Usability Audit, 3. Ergonomic & Accessibility Bottlenecks, 4. Inclusive Design Optimization Patches, 5. Mobile Ergonomics Scorecard (0-100). Maintain zero emojis.
agents.task:
Audit mobile ergonomics and accessibility across Krantind/Student-Voice. Focus on components/layout/Navbar.tsx (floating pill bottom tab bar), components/ui/Button.tsx, components/ui/Modal.tsx, components/feature/CommentInput.tsx, and app/globals.css (prefers-reduced-motion, scroll-slim, touch targets).

Key Mobile Patterns:
- Floating bottom pill tab bar on mobile (< 1024px) holding Feed, Search, Messages, Notifications, Profile.
- Responsive typography with clamp() scales.
- Focus visible outlines and touch target guidelines.
- prefers-reduced-motion media query disabling all keyframes and transitions for motion-sensitive users.
- ResponsiveContainer with fluid padding and max-w-content (72rem).

Evaluate:
1. Does the floating bottom tab bar stay within the natural thumb zone (Steven Hoober's thumb reach maps) on large mobile screens without obstructing bottom content or home gestures?
2. Do interactive elements (buttons, badge tags, comment triggers, poll choices) satisfy the minimum 44x44px Fitts's Law touch target?
3. Does the warm paper (#FAF7F2) and warm ink (#24201B) color pairing achieve WCAG AA/AAA contrast standards for outdoor campus sunlight readability?
4. How gracefully does the interface support neurodivergent students and users with motion sensitivity?
